pairs.registryProposal: Upward note for metric-identity: src/features/overview/libs/metricIdentity.ts:12-41 is a working instance of the technique's 'registry of declared variants' — three success-rate ids each naming source, window and derivation, resolved by one function. It also demonstrates the failure the technique should call out explicitly: a variant registry that omits unit, precision and polarity does not stop those three from forking, and polarity in particular immediately reappeared as a per-call-site boolean. Recommend the technique list those fields as required members of the registered variant, not just of the prose contract.

pairs.subject: embedded-preview
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/webbuild/preview_agent.rs:53 dispatches inbound bridge messages on shape alone (d.source !== "athena") with no e.origin check, and :61-64 and :80-83 post every reply and route report to the parent with a "*" wildcard target — the injection door and the symmetric leak the technique calls the bridge's only authentication layer.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/webbuild/preview_agent.rs:53 — the agent authenticates by envelope shape, which ships to the guest and is readable by any document in the frame tree; :61-64 and :80-83 address replies to "*", so a redirect or crash page in the frame receives the guest's location and element data.

src-tauri/src/webbuild/devserver.rs:77-78 sends the dev server's stdout and stderr to Stdio::null(), so a server that never becomes ready has no output to attach to the failure the technique requires be declared; and start() (:56-108) has no readiness deadline or verdict — the entry never moves to an unhealthy state, leaving the eternal loading frame as the user-visible outcome. Registration, one-server-per-project replacement, process-tree teardown and stop_all on exit (:44-171, :218-237) are otherwise exactly the pattern, and http_responds (:193-213) is a stronger readiness probe than the technique asks for.

src-tauri/src/webbuild/routes.rs:15-21 returns Ok(empty) when neither app/ nor src/app exists, and walk() (:25-27) swallows read_dir errors, so 'this guest matches no known convention' and 'a directory could not be read' both render as an app with no pages instead of the declared 'no routes discovered — navigate by URL'.

src-tauri/src/webbuild/versions.rs:23-34 — commit_snapshot discards the result of both git add and git commit and returns (), so a project whose snapshots quietly stopped committing looks identical to a protected one until the restore list comes up short; :43-45 likewise returns an empty version list when git fails. The capture boundary (per build turn) and the turn-summary label are correct, and restore (:65-83) is non-destructive.

src-tauri/src/webbuild/preview_agent.rs:62 echoes the request's reqId correctly, but the envelope carries no protocol version and the agent never announces a ready event, so the host cannot distinguish an absent agent from a stale one and a version mismatch is undetectable; the route events at :79-83 are also unthrottled at the source.

src-tauri/src/webbuild/preview_agent.rs:112-140 injects the agent as source into the guest's tree, re-adds it when a mutation drops it (:120-129) and skips a layout it cannot patch; the dev gate is structural (`process.env.NODE_ENV !== "development"` at :23 plus the build-time render gate at :146), the charter is two verbs with no evaluate, and :98-104 reaps every listener, the history patches and the highlight ring on teardown. The coarse fallback is real — plan.rs:36 carries the top/middle/bottom region anchoring used when the precise pointer is unavailable.
